query: Use /prototyping throughout this consultant session. Whenever a question presents visibly or behaviorally different choices, give me a local page where I can compare them before I answer.
Prototype three information architectures for this small team settings page so I can click through the alternatives and choose one. This is throwaway decision support, not app code.
Keep a single prototype URL growing as we work through this product workshop. Add each decision as another navigable step and remember which option I chose.
Resume the named quiet-dashboard prototyping session and add the next empty-state layout choice without touching sibling sessions.
For this grilling round, make throwaway comparisons for the queue layout and bulk-assignment behavior, but leave the naming question text-only.
I need to feel the difference between immediate undo, confirmation, and staged batch behavior before deciding. Build one disposable local interaction page for the comparison.
Turn these release notes into a durable self-contained HTML artifact, save it under my artifact home, and keep the verified local page available for later.
Build a polished product demo for tomorrow's sales call with a convincing narrative, seeded data, and a presentation-ready happy path.
Implement the selected settings-page direction in our Next.js app, wire it into the router, and add component tests.
Open the existing localhost app, click every navigation item, test keyboard behavior, and report bugs with screenshots.
Explain when teams should use prototypes versus wireframes. Give me a concise comparison and no files.
Create reusable Figma components for these three card layouts and publish them to our design-system library.
Use /prototyping for one step: compare a left rail, top tabs, and three columns for the dispatcher dashboard, recommend one, and give me the loopback link.
Stay in prototyping mode while the wayfinder tickets unfold. I want one paginated local session for every real visual or interaction decision, including text-only placeholders for the rest.
Sanity-check whether this state model feels right by making the three transition rules tangible on a throwaway interactive page before we choose one.
Show me three structurally different onboarding flows in a disposable page, let me switch among them, and stop before integrating the winner.
Make a durable dependency-free status dashboard from this CSV, store it as a named HTML artifact, and return its verified file path and URL.
Record a polished demo video of the existing checkout flow with narration and annotated callouts for the launch deck.
Fix the state-machine bug in src/checkout/reducer.ts and add regression tests for the invalid transition.
Generate a static PNG mockup of a futuristic analytics dashboard for the marketing site hero.
